metadata.question: Was there an active fire present near Paradise, California between November 7, 2018 to November 10, 2018?

data.raw_code: The user is asking about active fires near Paradise, California during November 7-10, 2018. This is a fire detection question, so I should use thermal anomaly data. Best datasets for this: 1. MODIS Active Fire (MCD14ML) - good for thermal anomalies 2. VIIRS Active Fire (VNP14IMGT) - higher resolution than MODIS 3. Landsat thermal bands - but might be overkill for simple fire detection I'll use VIIRS Active Fire data since it has good temporal coverage and resolution for this time period. Strategy: 1. Define geometry around Paradise, California 2. Use VIIRS Active Fire collection for the date range 3. Check if any fire pixels are detected in that area/time 4. Count the number of fire detections For fire detection, I don't need cloud masking since we're looking at thermal anomalies directly. I need to: - Check if collection is empty (C1) - Check if there are fire pixels (count > 0 = A, count = 0 = B) - Handle any calculation failures (C3) ```python import ee ee.Initialize(project='earthsense-436113') # 1. Geometry & Time Definitions paradise_ca = ee.Geometry.Point([-121.6219, 39.7596]) # Paradise, CA coordinates date_start = '2018-11-07' date_end = '2018-11-10' buffer_radius = 5000 # 5km buffer around Paradise # Create search area search_area = paradise_ca.buffer(buffer_radius) # 2. Data Acquisition - VIIRS Active Fire Data fire_collection = ee.ImageCollection('NOAA/VIIRS/001/VNP14IMGML') \ .filterBounds(search_area) \ .filterDate(date_start, date_end) # Check if collection is empty collection_size = fire_collection.size().getInfo() print(f"Fire detection images found: {collection_size}") if collection_size == 0: print("C1") else: # Get all fire detections in the collection fire_data = fire_collection.select('T21') # Count fire pixels (T21 > 0 indicates thermal anomaly) fire_count_img = fire_data.reduce(ee.Reducer.count()) # Get pixel count fire_count = fire_count_img.reduceRegion( reducer=ee.Reducer.sum(), geometry=search_area, scale=1000, maxPixels=1e9 ).get('T21').getInfo() print(f"Active fire pixels detected: {fire_count}") # Validate result if fire_count is None: print("C3") elif fire_count > 0: print("A") else: print("B") ```
data.code:
import ee
ee.Initialize(project='earthsense-436113')

# 1. Geometry & Time Definitions
paradise_ca = ee.Geometry.Point([-121.6219, 39.7596])  # Paradise, CA coordinates
date_start = '2018-11-07'
date_end = '2018-11-10'
buffer_radius = 5000  # 5km buffer around Paradise

# Create search area
search_area = paradise_ca.buffer(buffer_radius)

# 2. Data Acquisition - VIIRS Active Fire Data
fire_collection = ee.ImageCollection('NOAA/VIIRS/001/VNP14IMGML') \
    .filterBounds(search_area) \
    .filterDate(date_start, date_end)

# Check if collection is empty
collection_size = fire_collection.size().getInfo()
print(f"Fire detection images found: {collection_size}")

if collection_size == 0:
    print("<answer>C1</answer>")
else:
    # Get all fire detections in the collection
    fire_data = fire_collection.select('T21')
    
    # Count fire pixels (T21 > 0 indicates thermal anomaly)
    fire_count_img = fire_data.reduce(ee.Reducer.count())
    
    # Get pixel count
    fire_count = fire_count_img.reduceRegion(
        reducer=ee.Reducer.sum(),
        geometry=search_area,
        scale=1000,
        maxPixels=1e9
    ).get('T21').getInfo()
    
    print(f"Active fire pixels detected: {fire_count}")
    
    # Validate result
    if fire_count is None:
        print("<answer>C3</answer>")
    elif fire_count > 0:
        print("<answer>A</answer>")
    else:
        print("<answer>B</answer>")
